issues.description: The template's Bitmap24.hpp does not declare a default constructor, but the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines one and main.cpp uses it (Bitmap24 bitmap;). The solution repository's Bitmap24.hpp declares the default constructor. This mismatch in the template (missing constructor declaration) will cause compilation errors and confusion for students because the class is used with a default constructor but the header does not provide its declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the default constructor declaration to the template header to match the implementation and usage. For example, in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp add: 'Bitmap24();' (so the header declares both 'Bitmap24();' and 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);'). This will align the template with the implementation and the solution, avoiding compilation errors.
